omens.text: Your torches burn lower and bluer here, the flames hugging the wick with no draft to explain it.
The floor ahead is warmer underfoot than the one behind, warm as a hearthstone an hour after the fire.
The air smells faintly of rain on dry earth, a long way from any weather.
A sound from the room you just cleared, a boot on grit, comes back once, a fraction late.
The corridor ahead is no narrower than the last, yet your shoulders brush cold stone on both sides.
The chalk arrows you left on the way down sit a hand's width higher than you remember drawing them.
Dust lies soft and grey in the grooves of the stone, every one of them pointing the way you are going.
The torchlight reaches farther ahead than it does behind, where the dark sits close as a wall.
Your shadows lean toward the way down, long and thin across the floor, whatever the light says.
For a moment, in the quiet, all of you breathe in time, and the torch flame dips with each breath.
A slow pulse rises through the stone into the soles of your boots, slower than your own.
Looking back through the doorway, you find the room you cleared smaller than you remember, its far wall well inside the torchlight.
